chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

four men testified against a muhsan man for adultery, two of whom were considered just (mu'tadal) and the other two were not. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If they are four Muslims who are not known for perjury, their testimony is accepted in its entirety and the hadd punishment is carried out against the one they testified against. They are only required to testify to what they saw and knew, and it is upon the ruler (wali) to accept their testimony unless they are known for moral corruption (fisq).'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for accepting testimony from four witnesses in cases of adultery according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shafi'i and Shia juristic debate on whether the four witnesses in *hudud* cases must all be *adl* (just) or if the testimony is valid as long as none are known for perjury (*ghayr ma'rufin bil-fisq*). It emphasizes the ruler's (*al-wali*) duty to accept the collective testimony of four Muslim men who have directly witnessed the act, provided they are not disqualified by known moral corruption, thereby facilitating the enforcement of the stoning punishment for a *muhsan*.
